Didn't think I'd be so pro-Nolan but The Odyssey is one of my favorite films of the past few years. Certainly my favorite big budgeted fantasy movie I've seen in ages.

Anne Hathaway remains perfect

Overall, The Odyssey is a pretty great movie. Looks beautiful, interesting take on the material, casting ranges from perfect to "don't worry, he only got two lines", mostly OK sound mix (it is Nolan after all). But when Damon says "this Bronze Age we are living in is going to collapse" I lost it.

Frankly, taking the Odyssey and using it to talk about modern war morality as Nolan did is by far the wiser choice, I think. I get the desire to see the original text adapted faithfully as possible, but Nolan made the choices to make a more relevant film.
I only just learned that Polyphemus was a *20 ft tall puppet* in The Odyssey and just give Christopher Nolan all the money he needs to make movies forever. Just do it.

I’ve seen every Christopher Nolan movie since Memento besides The Odyssey, which I’m seeing next Wednesday, except for The Prestige, which fell through the cracks over the years for me somehow. That changes now.
